blocks.tex:
There is a second discrete curvature attached to a convex polygon: the
reciprocal radius of the inward circle tangent to three consecutive
supporting lines. Wegner's four-edge theorem concerns these radii
\cite{Wegner1994,Pak2010}. We give a converse as a companion to
\ref{thm:main}. The construction below uses a tangential polygon and
positive edge scaling; it is independent of the four-length system used for
the main theorem.

blocks.label: def:side-tangent-circle
blocks.title: def:side-tangent-circle
blocks.body:
Let $P_i$ be the vertices of a counterclockwise strictly convex polygon,
with outward unit normal $N_i$ on edge $[P_i,P_{i+1}]$.
The \emph{inward three-line circle at edge $i$} has center $C_i$ and radius
$r_i>0$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:side-tangent-distances}
 \langle N_{i-1},P_i-C_i\rangle
 =\langle N_i,P_i-C_i\rangle
 =\langle N_{i+1},P_{i+1}-C_i\rangle=r_i.\tag{8.1}\end{equation}
Its central contact is required to lie in the open edge $(P_i,P_{i+1})$.
The contacts on the two neighbouring supporting lines may lie on their
extensions. The circle need not be contained in the entire polygon.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.ThreeLineCircle
Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.IsSideTangentRealization
lean.code:
structure IsSideTangentRealization [NeZero n] (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ)
    (P N C : ZMod n → ℂ) : Prop where
  radius_pos : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i
  simple : IsSimplePolygon P
  strict_convex : StrictConvexEdgeSupport P
  unit_normal : ∀ i, ‖N i‖ = 1
  oriented_edge : ∀ i, ∃ ℓ : ℝ, 0 < ℓ ∧ P (i + 1) - P i = ℓ • (Complex.I * N i)
  supporting : ∀ i j, ⟪N i, P j - P i⟫_ℝ ≤ 0
  circles : ∀ i, ThreeLineCircle P N i (C i) (ρ i)
  unique_circle : ∀ i D r, ThreeLineCircle P N i D r → D = C i ∧ r = ρ i
  central_contact : ∀ i, C i + ρ i • N i ∈ openSegment ℝ (P i) (P (i + 1))

blocks.tex:
\href{../figures/tabachnikov-side-tangent-circle.svg}{Illustration: tabachnikov-side-tangent-circle}

The selected circle is tangent to three supporting lines, with
its central contact in the open edge. Here one neighbouring contact lies
beyond its edge. All coordinates, circle equations and contact parameters
in this example are checked with exact rational arithmetic.


Put $c_i=r_{i-1}-r_i$. By four cyclic sign changes we mean that there are
$i_1<i_2<i_3<i_4<i_1+n$ with
$c_{i_1}>0$, $c_{i_2}<0$, $c_{i_3}>0$ and $c_{i_4}<0$; zero differences are
retained but do not count as a sign. This formulation includes repeated
radii without a genericity assumption.

blocks.label: thm:side-tangent-converse
blocks.title: thm:side-tangent-converse
blocks.body:
Let $n\ge4$ and let $r_i>0$ be a cyclic sequence. Suppose that $r$ is
constant or that $c_i=r_{i-1}-r_i$ has four cyclic sign changes. Then a
simple strictly convex polygon realizes $r_i$ as the radii of its inward
three-line circles. Each center and radius are uniquely determined by the
three equations~\eqref{eq:side-tangent-distances}, and every central contact
lies in its open edge.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.IsSideTangentRealization.tangent_sphere
lean.code:
theorem IsSideTangentRealization.tangent_sphere [NeZero n]
    {ρ : ZMod n → ℝ} {P N C : ZMod n → ℂ} (h : IsSideTangentRealization ρ P N C)
    (i k : ZMod n) (hk : k = i - 1 ∨ k = i ∨ k = i + 1) :
    Metric.sphere (C i) (ρ i) ∩ supportingLine P N k = {C i + ρ i • N k} :=
  sphere_inter_normalLine (h.unit_normal k) (h.radius_pos i).le (h.circle_line_distance i k hk)

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.sideTangentConverse
lean.code:
theorem sideTangentConverse [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ)
    (h : SideTangentAdmissible ρ) : RealizesSideTangent ρ := by
  obtain ⟨hρ, hconst | hdfv⟩ := h
  · obtain ⟨r, hr⟩ := hconst
    exact sideTangentConverse_of_const hn ρ hρ hr
  · exact sideTangentConverse_of_dfv ρ hρ hdfv

deps.label: st:metric-tangency

blocks.tex:
The main ingredient is a balanced polygon circumscribed about the unit
circle. Its vertices, rather than the contact points, carry the coefficients.

blocks.label: lem:side-tangent-balance
blocks.title: lem:side-tangent-balance
blocks.body:
Suppose $\sum_i c_i=0$ and $c$ has four cyclic sign changes. There is a
strictly convex polygon $Y_i$, circumscribed about the unit circle with each
contact in its open edge, such that $\sum_i c_iY_i=0$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.isCyclicStrictTangentialFan_of_finite
lean.code:
theorem isCyclicStrictTangentialFan_of_finite [NeZero n] (s : ZMod n)
    {U Y : Fin n → ℂ} (h : IsStrictTangentialFan U Y) :
    IsCyclicStrictTangentialFan (fun i ↦ U ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i))
      (fun i ↦ Y ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)) := by
  refine ⟨fun i ↦ h.unit_normal _, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.normal_cross_pos ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.vertex_eq ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i j hji hjs
    apply h.strict_support
    · exact fun he ↦ hji ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective he)
    · intro he
      apply hjs
      apply (cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective
      simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using he
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.contact_interior ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.edge_pos ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i
    simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using h.edge_ne ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm i)
  · intro i j hji hjs
    simp only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ]
    apply h.cross_support
    · exact fun he ↦ hji ((cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective he)
    · intro he
      apply hjs
      apply (cyclicLabelEquiv s).symm.injective
      simpa only [cyclicLabelEquiv_symm_succ] using he

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.exists_balanced_strictTangentialFan
lean.code:
theorem exists_balanced_strictTangentialFan {n p q r : ℕ} [NeZero n]
    (hn : 4 ≤ n) (hp : 0 < p) (hpq : p < q) (hqr : q < r) (hr : r < n)
    (c : Fin n → ℝ) (hsum : ∑ i, c i = 0)
    (h₀ : 0 < c ⟨0, by omega⟩) (h₁ : c ⟨p, by omega⟩ < 0)
    (h₂ : 0 < c ⟨q, by omega⟩) (h₃ : c ⟨r, hr⟩ < 0) :
    ∃ U Y : Fin n → ℂ, IsStrictTangentialFan U Y ∧ ∑ i, c i • Y i = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨η, hη, hη₁, a, σ, ha, hσ, hsq, hd, hb⟩ :=
    exists_balanced_squareFan hn hp hpq hqr hr c hsum h₀ h₁ h₂ h₃
  exact ⟨fun i ↦ ProjectiveBall.transform a σ (normal (fanAngle n p q r η i)),
    fun i ↦ ProjectiveBall.transform a σ (fanVertex n p q r η i),
    projective_squareFan_isStrictTangentialFan hn hp hpq hqr hr hη hη₁.le ha hσ hsq hd, hb⟩

deps.title: Returning the balanced geometry to its original labels
deps.label: st:cyclic-fan

blocks.tex:
Choose four alternating nonzero coefficients, and place their labels at
$(1,1),(-1,1),(-1,-1),(1,-1)$ in that order. Collapse all intervening labels
to the corresponding side contact of the square. All labels and their
coefficients remain present. Denote this limiting configuration by $X_i$,
and consider the finite rational field
\[
 G(a)=\sum_i\frac{c_i X_i}{1-\langle a,X_i\rangle}.
\]
For sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, all denominators are positive on
$D_\varepsilon=\{(x,y):|x|+|y|\le1-\varepsilon\}$. On its upper boundary arc
$y\ge |x|$, one of the two upper corner denominators equals $\varepsilon$.
If the alternating corner coefficients are $\alpha,-\beta,\gamma,-\delta$
with $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta>0$, and the left and right contact
coefficients are $u,v$, then
\[
 \mathop{\rm Re}G(x,y)\ge
 \frac{\min(\alpha,\beta)}{\varepsilon}
       -\gamma-\delta-2|u|-2|v|>0.
\]
The upper and lower contact labels have zero horizontal contribution,
including near their poles. The corresponding bounds on the other three
arcs give, successively, $\mathop{\rm Im}G<0$ on the left,
$\mathop{\rm Re}G<0$ on the bottom and $\mathop{\rm Im}G>0$ on the right.
Thus the boundary field has winding number $-1$.

Now separate the repeated normals into small, strictly ordered clusters.
This produces a genuine tangential polygon $X_i^{\eta}$, with every edge
positive and every contact interior, converging to the labelled square as
$\eta\downarrow0$. Positivity of all denominators and the strict boundary
margins persist uniformly on the compact diamond. The perturbed field has
the same nonzero winding number and hence a zero $a$ in $D_\varepsilon$.
In particular $|a|<1$.

Set $\sigma=\sqrt{1-|a|^2}$ and
\[
 A=\sigma I+\frac{aa^{\mathsf T}}{1+\sigma},\qquad
 B_a(x)=\frac{Ax-a}{1-\langle a,x\rangle}.
\]
This projective transformation preserves the unit disk, its tangent lines,
and the cyclic order and open contacts of our polygon. All relevant
denominators are positive. Since $\sum_i c_i=0$,
\[
 \sum_i\frac{c_i}{1-\langle a,X_i^{\eta}\rangle}
 =\langle a,G(a)\rangle=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_i c_i B_a(X_i^{\eta})=A G(a)-a\langle a,G(a)\rangle=0.
\]
The vertices $Y_i=B_a(X_i^{\eta})$ have the required properties.

blocks.label: lem:side-tangent-scaling
blocks.title: lem:side-tangent-scaling
blocks.body:
Let $Y_i$ be a counterclockwise strictly convex polygon circumscribed about the unit circle,
with its contacts in its open edges. If $r_i>0$ and
$\sum_i(r_{i-1}-r_i)Y_i=0$, the cyclic edge equations
\begin{equation}\label{eq:side-tangent-scaling}
 P_{i+1}-P_i=r_i(Y_{i+1}-Y_i)\tag{8.2}\end{equation}
define a closed simple strictly convex polygon. Its inward three-line
circle at edge $i$ has center $C_i=P_i-r_iY_i$ and radius $r_i$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.sum_scaled_edges
lean.code:
lemma sum_scaled_edges [NeZero n] (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ) (Y : ZMod n → ℂ) :
    ∑ i, ρ i • (Y (i + 1) - Y i) = ∑ i, (ρ (i - 1) - ρ i) • Y i := by
  have he := Fintype.sum_equiv (Equiv.addRight (1 : ZMod n))
    (fun i ↦ ρ i • Y (i + 1)) (fun j ↦ ρ (j - 1) • Y j) (fun i ↦ by simp)
  simpa only [smul_sub, sub_smul, Finset.sum_sub_distrib] using
    congrArg (fun z : ℂ ↦ z - ∑ i, ρ i • Y i) he

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.strictSupport_of_positive_edge_scaling
lean.code:
theorem strictSupport_of_positive_edge_scaling [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    {P Y : ZMod n → ℂ} (hY : StrictConvexEdgeSupport Y) (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ)
    (hρ : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i) (hedge : ∀ i, P (i + 1) - P i = ρ i • (Y (i + 1) - Y i)) :
    StrictConvexEdgeSupport P := by
  have hs := isSimplePolygon_of_strictConvexEdgeSupport hn hY
  have ho := positiveOrientation_of_strictSupport hn hY
  have ht := hasPositiveTurningNumberOne_of_simple_positiveOrientation hs ho
  refine strictSupport_of_polar P (cyclicEdgeHeading Y)
    (fun k ↦ ρ (k : ZMod n) * cyclicEdgeLength Y k)
    (fun k ↦ mul_pos (hρ _) (cyclicEdgeLength_pos hs k))
    (cyclicEdgeHeading_strictMono hs ho) (cyclicEdgeHeading_succ_lt_add_pi hs ho)
    (cyclicEdgeHeading_add_n ht) ?_
  intro k
  have he : cyclicEdge P k = ρ (k : ZMod n) • cyclicEdge Y k := by
    simpa [cyclicEdge, cyclicVertex, Nat.cast_add] using hedge (k : ZMod n)
  rw [he, ← cyclicEdge_length_mul_exp_heading hs k]
  simp only [Complex.ofReal_mul, Complex.real_smul, mul_assoc]

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.realizesSideTangent_of_scaledFan
lean.code:
theorem realizesSideTangent_of_scaledFan [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n)
    (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ) (hρ : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i) {U Y P : ZMod n → ℂ}
    (hf : IsCyclicStrictTangentialFan U Y)
    (hedge : ∀ i, P (i + 1) - P i = ρ i • (Y (i + 1) - Y i))
    (hs : StrictConvexEdgeSupport P) (hp : IsSimplePolygon P) : RealizesSideTangent ρ := by
  let N : ZMod n → ℂ := fun i ↦ U (i + 1)
  let C : ZMod n → ℂ := fun i ↦ P i - ρ i • Y i
  have he : ∀ i, ∃ ℓ : ℝ, 0 < ℓ ∧ P (i + 1) - P i = ℓ • (Complex.I * N i) := by
    intro i
    obtain ⟨ℓ, hℓ, heq⟩ := hf.edge_pos i
    exact ⟨ρ i * ℓ, mul_pos (hρ i) hℓ, by rw [hedge i, heq, smul_smul]⟩
  refine ⟨P, N, C, hρ, hp, hs, fun i ↦ hf.unit_normal (i + 1), he,
    normal_support_of_strictSupport hs he, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro i
    simpa only [ThreeLineCircle, N, C, sub_add_cancel] using
      threeLineCircle_equations (hf.inner_left i) (hf.inner_right i) (hf.inner_right (i + 1))
        (hedge i)
  · intro i D r hD
    have heq : ⟪U i, P i - D⟫_ℝ = r ∧ ⟪U (i + 1), P i - D⟫_ℝ = r ∧
        ⟪U (i + 1 + 1), P (i + 1) - D⟫_ℝ = r := by
      simpa only [ThreeLineCircle, N, sub_add_cancel] using hD
    exact threeLineCircle_unique (hf.normal_cross_pos i).ne'
      (hf.inner_left i) (hf.inner_right i) (hf.inner_right (i + 1)) (hf.next_strict hn i)
      (hedge i) heq.1 heq.2.1 heq.2.2
  · intro i
    have hc := prescribedContact_mem_openSegment (ρ i) (hedge i) (hf.contact_interior i)
    simpa only [C, N, smul_sub, sub_add_eq_add_sub, add_sub_assoc] using hc

deps.title: Positive closed edge scaling retains strict support
deps.label: st:scaled-support

deps.title: Balance is exactly the edge-closure equation
deps.label: st:scaled-closure

deps.title: Scaled tangential geometry realizes the radii
deps.label: st:scaled-realization

blocks.tex:
Cyclic summation by parts gives
$\sum_i r_i(Y_{i+1}-Y_i)=\sum_i(r_{i-1}-r_i)Y_i=0$, so the edges close.
Positive scaling preserves their ordered directions and their total turn
of $2\pi$. For any fixed edge, the projections of the subsequent edges on
its left normal are first positive and then negative. Every intermediate
partial sum is positive, using closure for the second part. Hence every
nonincident vertex is strictly to its left. This gives strict support and
simplicity.

The outward normals satisfy
$\langle N_{i-1},Y_i\rangle=\langle N_i,Y_i\rangle=1$ and
$\langle N_{i+1},Y_{i+1}\rangle=1$. Substituting
$C_i=P_i-r_iY_i=P_{i+1}-r_iY_{i+1}$ gives all three
signed-distance equations. The central contact is the image of $N_i$ under
the positive homothety $x\mapsto C_i+r_ix$, and therefore lies in its open
edge. Adjacent normals are linearly independent. The first two equations
force any other center with radius $s$ to equal $P_i-sY_i$; the third then
gives $s=r_i$, since $\langle N_{i+1},Y_i\rangle<1$. Finally, unit normals
turn the signed-distance equations into actual circle tangency.

\href{../figures/tabachnikov-side-tangent-construction.svg}{Illustration: tabachnikov-side-tangent-construction}

A balanced polygon circumscribed about the unit circle (left) and
its positive edge scaling (right). The prescribed cyclic radii are
$(1,2,1,3/2,1,2,1,3/2)$. Closure, strict support and all eight circles are
verified exactly. The highlighted upper edge is the central edge of the
circle in \ref{fig:side-tangent-circle}.

\textbf{Proof of \ref{thm:side-tangent-converse}.} 
For nonconstant data, apply \ref{lem:side-tangent-balance} to
$c_i=r_{i-1}-r_i$, whose sum is zero, and then
\ref{lem:side-tangent-scaling}. For constant $r_i=r$, take a regular
polygon circumscribed about the unit circle and scale its edges by $r$.

The forward implication uses the signed affine-balance argument of
\cite[Section~21.6]{Pak2010}, with zero coefficients included. It is
Wegner's four-edge theorem, including zero differences, for the supporting-line
circles of \ref{def:side-tangent-circle}.

blocks.label: lem:side-tangent-signs
blocks.title: lem:side-tangent-signs
blocks.body:
Let $Y_i$ be the cyclic vertices of a counterclockwise strictly convex polygon. If
$\sum_i c_i=0$ and $\sum_i c_iY_i=0$, then either every $c_i=0$ or the cyclic
coefficient sequence has at least four sign changes.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.sideTangentForward
lean.code:
theorem sideTangentForward [NeZero n] (hn : 3 ≤ n) {ρ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    {P N C : ZMod n → ℂ} (h : IsSideTangentRealization ρ P N C) :
    SideTangentAdmissible ρ := by
  obtain ⟨Y, hY, hb⟩ := exists_strict_balanced_polygon_of_realization hn h
  refine ⟨h.radius_pos, ?_⟩
  rcases zero_or_dfv_of_strict_affine_balance hn hY (sum_radiusDifference ρ) hb with hz | hd
  · exact Or.inl (constant_of_radiusDifference_eq_zero hz)
  · exact Or.inr hd

deps.title: Wegner's condition for the actual radii
deps.label: st:forward

blocks.tex:
A nonzero zero-sum sequence has both signs. If it has no four alternating
signs, it has one nonpositive block and one nonnegative block, with zeros
allowed in either. Choose a negative entry $c_a$ beginning the first block
and a positive entry $c_b$ beginning the second, using cyclic lifts
$a<b<a+n$. The chord $Y_aY_b$ has strictly negative signed area against
vertices in $(a,b)$ and strictly positive signed area against those in
$(b,a+n)$. Thus
\[
 c_i[Y_a,Y_b,Y_i]\ge0\quad\hbox{for every }i,
 \qquad \sum_i c_i[Y_a,Y_b,Y_i]=0,
\]
where $[A,B,C]$ is the signed determinant. The equality follows from the
zero mass and zero vector sum, since the determinant is affine in its third
argument. Every summand vanishes. Strict chord separation forces all
coefficients except $c_a,c_b$ to vanish. The two balance equations then give
$c_a(Y_a-Y_b)=0$, contradicting $c_a<0$ and distinctness of the vertices.

blocks.label: cor:side-tangent-iff
blocks.title: cor:side-tangent-iff
blocks.body:
Let $n\ge4$ and $r_i>0$. The sequence $r$ is realized by the inward
three-line circles of a simple strictly convex polygon, with their central
contacts in the open edges, if and only if $r$ is constant or its cyclic
differences $r_{i-1}-r_i$ have at least four sign changes.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.realizesSideTangent_iff_admissible
lean.code:
theorem realizesSideTangent_iff_admissible [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) (ρ : ZMod n → ℝ) :
    RealizesSideTangent ρ ↔ SideTangentAdmissible ρ := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨P, N, C, h⟩
    exact sideTangentForward (by omega) h
  · exact sideTangentConverse hn ρ

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.SideTangent.realizesSideTangent_iff_dfv
lean.code:
theorem realizesSideTangent_iff_dfv [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) {ρ : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hρ : ∀ i, 0 < ρ i) (hnc : ¬ ∃ r, ∀ i, ρ i = r) :
    RealizesSideTangent ρ ↔ DFV (radiusDifference ρ) 0 := by
  rw [realizesSideTangent_iff_admissible hn]
  exact ⟨fun h ↦ h.2.resolve_left hnc, fun h ↦ ⟨hρ, Or.inr h⟩⟩

deps.title: Exact characterization of side-tangent radius words
deps.label: st:iff

blocks.tex:
Sufficiency is \ref{thm:side-tangent-converse}. For necessity, start
from the actual polygon and its circles, and set
$Y_i=(P_i-C_i)/r_i$. The two incident normal equations give
$\langle N_{i-1},Y_i\rangle=\langle N_i,Y_i\rangle=1$.
These normals are linearly independent, because the polygon is strictly
convex. The circle at the preceding edge satisfies the same two normalized
equations at $P_i$, so it gives the same $Y_i$. Consequently
\[
 Y_{i+1}-Y_i=\frac{P_{i+1}-P_i}{r_i}.
\]
This is a closed positive edge scaling of the original polygon; the strict
support argument in \ref{lem:side-tangent-scaling} therefore applies to
$Y$. Summation by parts gives
$\sum_i(r_{i-1}-r_i)Y_i=0$, and the differences themselves sum to zero.
\ref{lem:side-tangent-signs} supplies four sign changes unless every
difference vanishes. In the latter case the cyclic radius sequence is constant.
